evidence: Maren wedged the iron into the crack, then leveraged the dagger behind it. She braced her good foot against the floor, her injured shoulder bearing the strain. Her face flushed with effort, but she did not grunt. She pushed, then pulled, then pushed again. The stone groaned, a low, grinding sound that echoed faintly in the corridor.
Maren wrenched the stone free; it fell to the floor with a heavy thud, cracking the flagstone beneath it. The gap it left was dark and empty, revealing the rough, unworked stone behind the masonry.
"There," Maren said, wiping her brow with the back of her hand. "The trap is dead. The mechanism has nothing to rest on."
The group moved through the doorway, stepping carefully over the cracked flagstone.
